risks.note: DMR's delivery capacity is entirely people-led: 60 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026 for a consultancy that has executed close to 220 projects. Management states that 'our ability to attract, develop, retain, and effectively deploy a highly skilled workforce of engineering and management professionals significantly influences our operational efficiency, service quality, and long-term profitability', and the risk register's people row is mitigated only by 'the development of comprehensive career and talent development plans'. Loss of senior specialists directly removes revenue capacity and bid credibility.
risks.risk: Human-capital dependency - the business has no assets other than its engineers

risks.note: AGM Item No. 7 records that 'the Company has identified significant business opportunities in the areas of Engineering Consulting, EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) Services, Power Trading Services including cross-border power trading, and Renewable Energy Power Generation, Energy Storage and Transmission businesses, in accordance with the applicable guidelines, rules and regulations issued by CERC/SERC and other regulatory authorities.' EPC, power trading and generation carry balance-sheet, execution and CERC/SERC licensing exposures the current fee-based consultancy does not, and the Company discloses no capital commitment to fund them.
risks.risk: Diversification into capital-intensive, regulated adjacencies well outside the asset-light consultancy model

risks.note: The MD&A financial-risk row explicitly names 'Taxation Risks, Market Risk, Foreign Currency Risk, Credit Risk, Liquidity Risk, Operational Risk, Country Risk'. These are live rather than theoretical: operations run in Bhutan, Laos and Africa, a US subsidiary (DMR Consulting USA Inc., Cupertino) is held 100% but the investment into it 'is pending due to regulatory measures', and the newly identified opportunity set includes cross-border power trading. Mitigation is described only as a generic four-stage identify-analyse-decide-monitor process.
risks.risk: Country, foreign-currency and cross-border exposure from international operations

risks.note: Credit risk and liquidity risk are named in the MD&A financial-risk row. The revenue base is B2B and concentrated in EPC agencies, PSUs and IPPs whose own payment cycles are project- and approval-driven, so realisation timing sits outside the Company's control while its cost base (salaried engineers) is fixed.
risks.risk: Client credit and collection risk in a fee-based, project-linked model

risks.note: The risk register carries a dedicated Employee Health & Safety row, noting that a healthy and safe working environment affects productivity, retention and reputation. The exposure is structural for this business: during FY 2025-26 experts and engineers travelled to remote locations in Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram, Bhutan, Laos and Africa, and the lender-engineering team travels extensively across India. Mitigation is limited to awareness and training programmes, physical/psychological support and medical insurance for permanent employees.
risks.risk: Employee health and safety exposure from remote-site and international field work

risks.note: The risk register states that 'climate change is a threat to the Company's infrastructure that may disrupt operations and potentially impact the safety and well-being of employees', mitigated by a business continuity policy and emergency response plans. For a firm whose assignments sit on Himalayan hydropower, dam and tunnel sites, weather and hydrological disruption is a direct project-delivery and site-access risk.
risks.risk: Climate change as a threat to operations and personnel

risks.note: The register flags that 'non-compliance to ABAC requirements or fraud instances can expose an organization to reputational and financial damage', with integrity described as critical to safeguarding market confidence and client trust. The Company bids for PSU and government-linked infrastructure work in India and overseas, where procurement-integrity failures can result in disqualification as well as reputational loss. Mitigation is the DMR Business Code of Conduct plus an ABAC programme.

capex_expansion.body: DMR is an asset-light engineering consultancy and discloses no manufacturing capacity, no plant additions and no rupee capex programme anywhere in this bundle; the named capital-commitments disclosure explicitly states that no capital commitment exists as at the financial-statement date. - Comprehensive whole-lifecycle service portfolio - design and engineering, due diligence and regulatory advisory, bid management, …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- DMR's delivery capacity is entirely people-led: 60 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026 for a consultancy that has executed close to 220 projects. Management states that 'our ability to attract, develop, retain, and effectively deploy a highly skilled workforce of engineering and management professionals significantly influences our operational efficiency, service quality, and long-term profitability', and the risk register's people row is mitigated only by 'the development of comprehensive career and talent development plans'. Loss of senior specialists directly removes revenue capacity and bid credibility.
- AGM Item No. 7 records that 'the Company has identified significant business opportunities in the areas of Engineering Consulting, EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) Services, Power Trading Services including cross-border power trading, and Renewable Energy Power Generation, Energy Storage and Transmission businesses, in accordance with the applicable guidelines, rules and regulations issued by CERC/SERC and other regulatory authorities.' EPC, power trading and generation carry balance-sheet, execution and CERC/SERC licensing exposures the current fee-based consultancy does not, and the Company discloses no capital commitment to fund them.
- The MD&A financial-risk row explicitly names 'Taxation Risks, Market Risk, Foreign Currency Risk, Credit Risk, Liquidity Risk, Operational Risk, Country Risk'. These are live rather than theoretical: operations run in Bhutan, Laos and Africa, a US subsidiary (DMR Consulting USA Inc., Cupertino) is held 100% but the investment into it 'is pending due to regulatory measures', and the newly identified opportunity set includes cross-border power trading. Mitigation is described only as a generic four-stage identify-analyse-decide-monitor process.
- Credit risk and liquidity risk are named in the MD&A financial-risk row. The revenue base is B2B and concentrated in EPC agencies, PSUs and IPPs whose own payment cycles are project- and approval-driven, so realisation timing sits outside the Company's control while its cost base (salaried engineers) is fixed.
- The risk register carries a dedicated Employee Health & Safety row, noting that a healthy and safe working environment affects productivity, retention and reputation. The exposure is structural for this business: during FY 2025-26 experts and engineers travelled to remote locations in Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram, Bhutan, Laos and Africa, and the lender-engineering team travels extensively across India. Mitigation is limited to awareness and training programmes, physical/psychological support and medical insurance for permanent employees.
- The risk register states that 'climate change is a threat to the Company's infrastructure that may disrupt operations and potentially impact the safety and well-being of employees', mitigated by a business continuity policy and emergency response plans. For a firm whose assignments sit on Himalayan hydropower, dam and tunnel sites, weather and hydrological disruption is a direct project-delivery and site-access risk.
- The register flags that 'non-compliance to ABAC requirements or fraud instances can expose an organization to reputational and financial damage', with integrity described as critical to safeguarding market confidence and client trust. The Company bids for PSU and government-linked infrastructure work in India and overseas, where procurement-integrity failures can result in disqualification as well as reputational loss. Mitigation is the DMR Business Code of Conduct plus an ABAC programme.
- A corporate-governance risk row is carried in the register, noting that governance failures 'can result in reputation loss and damage to stakeholder trust and business disruption', mitigated by periodical internal reviews, audits and regulatory-change presentations. The board is in the middle of a substantial transition - Mr. Man Mohan Madan appointed 28 February 2026, and Mr. Divay Mittal and Mr. Arvind Bhat on 9 May 2026, all still pending shareholder regularisation - while the promoter Managing Director and family members (Smt. Neelam Mittal, Whole-time Director; Mr. Divay Mittal) hold executive positions. The AR itself carries internal inconsistencies in these disclosures (Mr. Divay Mittal shown with two different DINs; director terms printed as 'five (2) years').
